---
title: "group_split() puts the groups in alphabetical order"
ref: TDY-10
categories: [tidyverse]

attendu: "the row for Switzerland"
versions: "All versions of {dplyr}"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2020)"

::: {.piege packages="dplyr"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))

sales <- data.frame(country = c("Switzerland", "Austria", "France"), n = 1:3)
pieces <- group_split(sales, country)
names(pieces) <- unique(sales$country)
pieces$Switzerland
```
:::

## Why

`group_split()` returns an unnamed list, in group order, that is sorted by the key: Austria, France, Switzerland. That is not the order in which they appear in the data. Naming the list with `unique()`, which follows the order of appearance, shifts every name, and each piece bears the name of another country.

For a factor column, the order is that of the levels, which does not make things simpler.

## The fix

Take the names from `group_keys()`, which follows the same order as `group_split()`, or use base R's `split()`, which names the list itself.

::: {.piege packages="dplyr"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))

groups <- group_by(sales, country)
pieces <- group_split(groups)
names(pieces) <- group_keys(groups)$country
pieces$Switzerland

split(sales, f = sales$country)$Switzerland
```
:::
